answer: Ledge-based Sybil Resistance requires each identity to plant a physical marker on a shared ledge, enforced by a verification protocol that cross-checks GPS and biometric data. Attackers face a per-identity cost of maintaining unique physical ledge markers under constant gale conditions, making mass fake identities economically unfeasible. The trellis of cross-referenced environmental sensors ensures no two identities can occupy the same ledge without detection.
